name: plugins
description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins
one_liner: The official rulebook and example set for building add-ons that let the Cursor AI coding assistant talk to other business tools like Gmail, Salesforce, or HubSpot.
buyer: A SaaS company's developer-relations or integrations team that wants their product reachable from inside AI coding tools but has no spare engineering time to build it.
business_use_cases: A dev agency builds and maintains a custom Cursor plugin for a SaaS vendor's product (like the existing Salesforce, Gong, or Intercom plugins) as a paid integration project.
An integrations contractor offers 'get your SaaS product listed as an official-style Cursor plugin' as a fixed-price package aimed at smaller B2B tool vendors.
An internal platform team at a company builds a private Cursor plugin for their own internal tools, saving engineers from re-explaining internal APIs to the AI each session.

money_ideas.idea: Fixed-fee contract to build and publish a vendor-specific Cursor plugin
Ongoing maintenance retainer to keep a published plugin working as Cursor's spec evolves

steal_this: Build a Cursor plugin for a mid-size SaaS tool that doesn't have one yet, publish it, then cold-email that company's DevRel team offering to hand over or maintain it for a fee.
